sections.kicker: Prepared for Axkan Taller by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site and your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Axkan has a story no one else can tell. The captions leave it out.
sections.keep: The black and white garment portraits. They look like one brand and nobody else's.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet
first.

pins.what: The bio lists four businesses in one line.
pins.why: A new visitor cannot tell if Axkan is a clothing label, a gallery or a school.
pins.how: Pick the one thing Axkan is first and let the others hang from it.
pins.label: Your bio
pins.cost: Visitors file it under the nearest category, a shop with nice textiles.

pins.what: Several captions are hashtags and nothing else.
pins.why: The people, the valley and the loom behind the pieces never speak, so they look like any handwoven textile.
pins.how: Let one sentence of the story lead, and keep the tags small.
pins.label: Your captions
pins.cost: Hashtags describe the category. Only the story says why Axkan and not another weaver.

pins.quote: tejidas en telar de pedal en los Valles Centrales de Oaxaca y bordadas a mano por mujeres Wixárikas de la Sierra Norte de Jalisco
pins.what: One older caption holds the real story: Oaxaca weavers and Wixárika embroiderers on the same piece.
pins.why: Two living traditions on one garment is something no other label can claim.
pins.how: Give that collaboration its own name and its own place at the top of the grid.
pins.label: Your caption
pins.cost: The strongest fact about the work sits in a caption from an old post.
